regulations.description: General requirements for basic safety and essential performance of medical electrical equipment
Standard for Y capacitors referenced in MOPP requirements

tests.requirement: Voltage to earth or to other ACCESSIBLE PARTS did not exceed 42.4 V peak a.c. or 60 V d.c. for parts inside ACCESS COVER in NORMAL or single fault condition
Limit of 60 V d.c. applied with no more than 10% peak-to-peak ripple; when ripple larger than specified, 42.4 V peak limit applied
Energy did not exceed 240 VA for longer than 60 s or stored energy available did not exceed 20 J at a potential of 2 V or more
LEAKAGE CURRENT limits applied when voltages higher than limits in 8.4.2 c) were present
tests.result: Not higher than limits in 8.4.2 c).

Internal parts touchable by metal test rod (diameter 4 mm, length 100 mm) inserted through openings on top of ENCLOSURE or through openings for adjustment of pre-set controls in NORMAL USE
Test pin or test rod inserted through relevant openings with minimal force of no more than 1 N
Test rod inserted in every possible position through openings for pre-set controls adjustable in NORMAL USE, with force of 10 N
Test repeated with TOOL specified in instructions for use
Test rod freely and vertically suspended through openings on top of ENCLOSURE
Devices used to de-energize parts when ACCESS COVER opened without TOOL comply with 8.11.1 for mains isolating switches and remain effective in SINGLE FAULT CONDITION
A TOOL is required when it is possible to prevent the devices from operating
Worst case voltage between pins of plug and between either supply pin and ENCLOSURE did not exceed 60 V one second after disconnecting the plug of ME EQUIPMENT or its parts
When voltage exceeded 60 V, calculated or measured stored charge did not exceed 45 μC
Separation of parts
MEANS OF PROTECTION (MOP)
Two MEANS OF PROTECTION provided for ME EQUIPMENT to prevent APPLIED and other ACCESSIBLE PARTS from exceeding limits in 8.4
A MEANS OF PROTECTION protecting APPLIED PARTS or parts identified by 4.6 considered as MEANS OF PATIENT PROTECTION
Each MEANS OF PROTECTION categorized as MOPP or MOOP per Clause 4.6 and flow chart in Fig A.12
Varnishing, enamelling, oxidation, and similar protective finishes/coatings re-plasticizing at operational/sterilization temperatures disregarded as MEANS OF PROTECTION
Components and wiring forming a MEANS OF PROTECTION comply with 8.10
Insulation, CREEPAGE, CLEARANCES, components or earth connections not complying with 8.5.1.2 and 8.5.1.3 not considered as MEANS OF PROTECTION; failure of these parts regarded as NORMAL CONDITION

CREEPAGE and CLEARANCES forming MOPP complied with Table 12

A Y (Y1 or Y2) capacitor complying with IEC 60384-14 considered one MEANS OF PATIENT PROTECTION

semantic_fragments.content: For parts inside an ACCESS COVER that can be opened without a TOOL, or where a TOOL is needed but the instructions for use instruct an OPERATOR other than SERVICE PERSONNEL to open the relevant ACCESS COVER: voltage to earth or to other ACCESSIBLE PARTS must not exceed 42.4 V peak a.c. or 60 V d.c. in NORMAL or single fault condition. The 60 V d.c. limit applies with no more than 10% peak-to-peak ripple; when ripple is larger, the 42.4 V peak limit applies. Energy must not exceed 240 VA for longer than 60 s or stored energy must not exceed 20 J at a potential of 2 V or more.

Internal parts touchable by test pin in Fig 8 inserted through an opening in an ENCLOSURE, and internal parts touchable by a metal test rod with a diameter of 4 mm and a length of 100 mm inserted through any opening on top of ENCLOSURE or through openings provided for adjustment of pre-set controls by the RESPONSIBLE ORGANIZATION in NORMAL USE using a TOOL, are subject to voltage and energy limits of 8.4.2 c). Test pin or rod inserted with minimal force of no more than 1 N through relevant openings. Test rod inserted in every possible position through openings for pre-set controls adjustable in NORMAL USE with force of 10 N. Test repeated with TOOL specified in instructions for use. Test rod freely and vertically suspended through openings on top of ENCLOSURE.

Two MEANS OF PROTECTION are required for ME EQUIPMENT to prevent APPLIED and other ACCESSIBLE PARTS from exceeding limits in 8.4. Each MEANS OF PROTECTION must be categorized as either a MEANS OF PATIENT PROTECTION (MOPP) or a MEANS OF OPERATOR PROTECTION (MOOP), taking into account Clause 4.6 and the flow chart in Fig A.12. Varnishing, enamelling, oxidation, and similar protective finishes and coatings with sealing compounds re-plasticizing at temperatures expected during operation and sterilization are disregarded as MEANS OF PROTECTION. Components and wiring forming a MEANS OF PROTECTION must comply with 8.10. Insulation, CREEPAGE, CLEARANCES, components or earth connections not complying with 8.5.1.2 and 8.5.1.3 are not considered as MEANS OF PROTECTION, and failure of these parts is regarded as NORMAL CONDITION.

MEANS OF PATIENT PROTECTION (MOPP) requirements under 8.5.1.2: Solid insulation forming a MOPP must comply with dielectric strength test of Clause 8.8 at the test voltage specified in Table 6. CREEPAGE and CLEARANCES forming a MOPP must comply with Table 12. PROTECTIVE EARTH CONNECTIONS forming a MOPP must comply with Cl. 8.6. A Y (Y1 or Y2) capacitor complying with IEC 60384-14 is considered one MEANS OF PATIENT PROTECTION. A single Y1 capacitor may be used for two MEANS OF PATIENT PROTECTION when the working voltage is less than 42.4 V peak a.c. or 60 V d.c.
